newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end mixed in quiet pre-holiday dealings.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end mixed in quiet pre-holiday dealings.

text.p: U.S. stocks drifted to a mixed finish after last week's strong gains, with volume thinned by the absence of many players before the Christmas Day holiday on Wednesday.

"It's the hangover after the wild ride of (triple witching) options expirations last week. I think a lot of players are done for the rest of the year," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
After surging 180 points last week, the Dow industrials rose five to about 6489.

Losers outpaced gainers 13-11 on NYSE volume of about 340 million shares, the lowest since 322 million shares changed hands on October 14. Activity on Monday was a far cry from the frenetic pace on Friday, when some 650 million shares were traded.
U.S. stock markets will hold an abbreviated session on Tuesday, when trading will end at 1300 EST/1800 GMT. U.S. financial markets will be closed on Wednesday, Christmas Day.

The Nasdaq Composite remained weak for much of the day, falling nine to about 1279. Computer makers were under pressure amid concerns about holiday PC sales, analysts said. Compaq fell four to 72-3/4 and Dell Computer lost 3-1/4 to 51-3/4.
"There are some concerns about retail sales for PCs which have been anything but robust," said Prudential Securities market analyst Bill Meehan.
"But it's not surprising for techs to give back some gains. Some of them have had huge moves," he said.
Among other tech issues, IBM slipped 3/8 to 154-1/8, Intel shed 2-3/8 to 132-1/4 and ThreeCom was off 7/16 to 76-7/16.

Energy companies drew buying interest after Morgan Stanley raised its 1997 estimates for crude and natural gas prices and upgraded a handful of energy stocks. Louis Dreyfus rose one to 17-5/8, and YPF added one to 24-7/8 in U.S. trading.
USX-Marathon rose 1-1/8 to 25, and Enron inched up 1/8 to 25-7/8. Apache, which Morgan downgraded, lost one to 36-1/2.
Analysts expect slower activity as the week progresses. "We're trading in a vacuum. The market was pretty dull," Meehan said.

Among individual stocks, Pacific Gas & Electric lost 1-3/8 to 21-5/8. After a call with company officials, EVEREN Securities cut its fiscal 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates to reflect higher effective tax rates. Smith Barney downgraded the stock.
U.S. Diagnostic lost 2-11/16 to 9-3/8. Bear Stearns dropped its buy rating on the stock.

WorldCom rose 1-1/8 to 23-1/4 amid continued takeover speculation. But industry analysts said the cost of buying the company and likely earnings dilution for any buyer made a bid unlikely. Meanwhile, WorldCom's takeover of MFS Communications was approved by shareholders, MFS said.
Claire's Stores lost 2-3/4 to 11-3/4. PaineWebber and Raymond James cut earnings estimates, citing weak sales.
Genzyme lost 2-3/8 to 23-1/8. Cowen cut its 1997 earnings estimate for the biotech company to $1.20 a share from $1.40.
Cabletron lost 4-1/2 to 36 after reporting quarterly earnings rose to $0.46 a share, in line with expectations.
Some investors were hoping for an upside surprise.
Home Beneficial surged 8-11/16 to 37-15/16 after American General Corp, off 1/4 to 40, agreed to acquire it for $39 a share, or $665 million in either cash or stock.
Roosevelt Financial rose 2-25/64 to 20-33/64 after Mercantile Bancorp Inc, off one to 49-3/4, said it would acquire Roosevelt in a $1.1 billion stock and cash deal.
W.R. Grace added 1-3/8 to 50 after agreeing to sell its cocoa business to Archer Daniels Midland, up 1/2 to 22-7/8, for about $430 million in cash and the assumption of debt.
The S&P 500 fell 1.95 to 746.92.
The NYSE Composite fell 0.82 to 393.29
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
